metadata.description: FeliNet golden evaluation dataset for RAG pipeline benchmarking
metadata.notes: Each test case has: query, expected_answer (gold standard), expected_source (which data source should be retrieved), content_type, and difficulty level.

test_cases.query: What are the symptoms of chronic kidney disease in cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Symptoms of chronic kidney disease in cats include increased thirst and urination, decreased appetite, weight loss, lethargy, nausea, vomiting, and an unkempt appearance. In advanced stages, cats may develop high blood pressure and anemia.

test_cases.query: How is feline diabetes diagnosed and treated?
test_cases.expected_answer: Feline diabetes is diagnosed through blood tests showing persistently elevated blood glucose levels and the presence of glucose in the urine. Treatment typically involves insulin injections, dietary management with high-protein low-carbohydrate food, and regular monitoring of blood glucose levels.

test_cases.query: What is feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) and is it contagious?
test_cases.expected_answer: FIP is a viral disease caused by certain strains of feline coronavirus. While feline coronavirus is common and usually causes mild symptoms, in rare cases it mutates into the FIP-causing form. FIP itself is not considered highly contagious between cats, but the underlying coronavirus is easily spread.

test_cases.query: What vaccines are recommended for indoor cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Core vaccines recommended for all cats including indoor cats are: panleukopenia (feline distemper), feline herpesvirus, calicivirus, and rabies. These are considered essential regardless of lifestyle. Non-core vaccines like feline leukemia virus (FeLV) may be recommended based on risk assessment.

test_cases.query: What are the signs of hyperthyroidism in cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Signs of hyperthyroidism in cats include weight loss despite increased appetite, increased thirst and urination, hyperactivity, vomiting, diarrhea, and an unkempt coat. It is most common in middle-aged to older cats and is caused by an overproduction of thyroid hormones.

test_cases.query: How does feline leukemia virus (FeLV) spread between cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: FeLV spreads primarily through close contact between cats, including mutual grooming, shared food and water bowls, and bite wounds. It can also be transmitted from mother to kittens during pregnancy, nursing, or grooming. The virus is present in saliva, nasal secretions, urine, feces, and blood.

test_cases.query: What causes urinary tract problems in cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Feline lower urinary tract disease (FLUTD) can be caused by several factors including urinary stones, urinary tract infections, urethral obstruction, and feline idiopathic cystitis (the most common cause). Stress, diet, obesity, and insufficient water intake can contribute to urinary problems.

test_cases.query: What is feline asthma and how is it treated?
test_cases.expected_answer: Feline asthma is a chronic inflammatory condition of the airways that causes difficulty breathing, wheezing, and coughing. Treatment typically involves corticosteroids to reduce inflammation and bronchodilators to open the airways. These can be administered orally, by injection, or via inhaler.

test_cases.query: Can cats get heartworm disease?
test_cases.expected_answer: Yes, cats can get heartworm disease from infected mosquito bites. While less common in cats than dogs, heartworm disease in cats can be serious and even fatal. There is no approved treatment for heartworm infection in cats, making prevention especially important.

test_cases.query: What are the symptoms of feline upper respiratory infections?
test_cases.expected_answer: Symptoms of feline upper respiratory infections include sneezing, nasal discharge, congestion, conjunctivitis, eye discharge, fever, loss of appetite, and lethargy. Most upper respiratory infections are caused by feline herpesvirus or feline calicivirus.

test_cases.query: How do you prevent ringworm in cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Ringworm prevention involves keeping the environment clean, isolating infected cats, regular cleaning and disinfection of the home, and treating all animals in the household if one is infected. Ringworm is a fungal infection (not a worm) that can spread to humans.

test_cases.query: What is feline panleukopenia and how severe is it?
test_cases.expected_answer: Feline panleukopenia (feline distemper) is a highly contagious and potentially fatal viral disease. It attacks rapidly dividing cells in the body, particularly in the bone marrow and intestines. Symptoms include severe vomiting, diarrhea, dehydration, and a dangerously low white blood cell count. Kittens are especially vulnerable.

test_cases.query: What dental problems are common in cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Common dental problems in cats include periodontal disease, tooth resorption, stomatitis, and gingivitis. Tooth resorption is particularly common and involves the gradual destruction of tooth structure. Signs include difficulty eating, drooling, and pawing at the mouth.

test_cases.query: How is FIV different from FeLV in cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: FIV (Feline Immunodeficiency Virus) and FeLV (Feline Leukemia Virus) are both retroviruses but differ in key ways. FIV primarily spreads through bite wounds and progresses slowly, while FeLV spreads through casual contact and tends to cause more severe disease more quickly. FIV-positive cats can live many years with proper care, while FeLV-positive cats generally have a shorter life expectancy.

test_cases.query: What causes cancer in cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Cancer in cats can be caused by various factors including genetic predisposition, viral infections (particularly FeLV), environmental factors, and age. Lymphoma is one of the most common cancers in cats, and FeLV-positive cats have a significantly higher risk of developing it.

test_cases.query: What is the temperament of a Maine Coon cat?
test_cases.expected_answer: Maine Coons are known as gentle giants with a friendly, sociable temperament. They are often described as dog-like in their loyalty and playfulness. They are intelligent, good with children and other pets, and enjoy interactive play. They are also known for their chirping vocalizations.

test_cases.query: How big do Ragdoll cats get?
test_cases.expected_answer: Ragdoll cats are one of the largest domesticated cat breeds. Males typically weigh between 15-20 pounds and females between 10-15 pounds. They are slow to mature, reaching full size and coat development around 3-4 years of age. They are known for their large blue eyes and semi-long silky coat.

test_cases.query: What health issues are Siamese cats prone to?
test_cases.expected_answer: Siamese cats are prone to several health issues including progressive retinal atrophy, amyloidosis (liver disease), asthma, and certain heart conditions. They may also be predisposed to some cancers. Their crossed eyes and kinked tails, once common breed traits, have been largely bred out.

test_cases.query: What is unique about the Scottish Fold cat's appearance?
test_cases.expected_answer: Scottish Fold cats are distinguished by their folded ears, which bend forward and down due to a natural genetic mutation affecting cartilage. Not all Scottish Folds have folded ears - some have straight ears. The fold gene can also affect cartilage throughout the body, which is why breeding two folded-ear cats together is discouraged.

test_cases.query: What are the characteristics of a Bengal cat?
test_cases.expected_answer: Bengal cats are known for their distinctive spotted or marbled coat pattern that resembles wild cats like the Asian leopard cat, from which they were originally bred. They are highly active, intelligent, and playful. They enjoy water more than most cat breeds and need plenty of mental stimulation and exercise.

test_cases.query: What is the origin of the Persian cat breed?
test_cases.expected_answer: The Persian cat is one of the oldest cat breeds, originating from Persia (modern-day Iran). They were brought to Europe in the 1600s and became popular in the Victorian era. They are known for their long, luxurious coat, flat face, and calm, gentle temperament.

test_cases.query: How long do Sphynx cats live?
test_cases.expected_answer: Sphynx cats typically live 8-14 years, though some can live longer with proper care. Despite their hairless appearance, they require regular bathing to remove oil buildup on their skin. They are known for being energetic, social, and seeking warmth from their owners.

test_cases.query: What is special about the Abyssinian cat breed?
test_cases.expected_answer: Abyssinian cats are one of the oldest known cat breeds, characterized by their ticked tabby coat pattern where each hair has multiple bands of color. They are highly active, curious, and intelligent cats that enjoy climbing and exploring. They are often described as one of the most dog-like cat breeds.

test_cases.query: Are Russian Blue cats good for people with allergies?
test_cases.expected_answer: Russian Blue cats are sometimes recommended for people with allergies because they are believed to produce less of the Fel d 1 protein, which is the primary cat allergen. However, no cat breed is truly hypoallergenic. Russian Blues have a dense double coat that may trap more allergens close to the skin.

test_cases.query: What is the Norwegian Forest Cat known for?
test_cases.expected_answer: The Norwegian Forest Cat is a large, sturdy breed adapted to cold climates with a thick, waterproof double coat. They are excellent climbers with strong claws. They originate from Northern Europe and feature in Norse mythology. They are friendly, independent, and good with families.

test_cases.query: What are the CFA breed standards for the British Shorthair?
test_cases.expected_answer: The CFA breed standard for the British Shorthair describes a compact, well-balanced cat with a broad chest, strong legs, and a round head with full cheeks. The coat should be short, dense, and firm to the touch. The most recognized color is British Blue, though many colors are accepted.

test_cases.query: What is the Birman cat breed standard according to CFA?
test_cases.expected_answer: According to CFA, the Birman is a color-pointed cat with a long, silky coat that does not mat. They have distinctive white gloves on all four paws. They have a Roman-shaped nose, blue eyes, and a medium-long stocky body. The Birman is known for being gentle, affectionate, and social.

test_cases.query: How much protein does a cat need in its diet?
test_cases.expected_answer: Cats are obligate carnivores and require a high-protein diet. Adult cats need a minimum of about 26% protein in their diet on a dry matter basis, though many experts recommend higher levels. Protein provides essential amino acids like taurine that cats cannot synthesize on their own.

test_cases.query: Can cats drink milk?
test_cases.expected_answer: Most adult cats are lactose intolerant and drinking cow's milk can cause digestive upset including diarrhea and stomach pain. Kittens produce the enzyme lactase to digest their mother's milk, but this ability typically decreases after weaning. If you want to give cats a milk treat, specially formulated cat milk is available.

test_cases.query: What should I feed a kitten?
test_cases.expected_answer: Kittens should be fed a complete and balanced kitten food that is higher in calories, protein, and certain nutrients than adult cat food to support their rapid growth. They should be fed multiple small meals throughout the day. Kittens can transition to adult food around 12 months of age.

test_cases.query: Is a raw food diet safe for cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Raw food diets for cats are controversial. Proponents claim benefits like shinier coats and better dental health, but veterinary organizations generally advise against raw diets due to risks of bacterial contamination (Salmonella, E. coli) and nutritional imbalances that can harm both cats and their human families.

test_cases.query: How much water should a cat drink per day?
test_cases.expected_answer: Cats should drink approximately 4 ounces of water per 5 pounds of body weight daily. Cats on wet food diets get much of their water from food, while cats on dry food need to drink more. Insufficient water intake can contribute to urinary tract problems and kidney issues.

test_cases.query: What nutrients are essential for cats that they can't produce themselves?
test_cases.expected_answer: Cats require several nutrients they cannot synthesize, most importantly taurine (an amino acid essential for heart and eye health), arachidonic acid (a fatty acid), vitamin A (cats cannot convert beta-carotene), and niacin. Taurine deficiency can lead to serious heart disease and blindness.

test_cases.query: Is grain-free cat food better for cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Grain-free cat food is not necessarily better for cats. Most cats can digest grains without issues. The important factor is that the food is nutritionally complete and balanced. Some grain-free diets substitute grains with other carbohydrates like potatoes or peas, which may not offer nutritional advantages.

test_cases.query: How can I help my overweight cat lose weight?
test_cases.expected_answer: To help an overweight cat lose weight, work with your veterinarian to determine a target weight and calorie intake. Gradually reduce food portions, switch to a weight management formula, increase play and exercise, use puzzle feeders, and avoid free-feeding. Weight loss should be gradual to avoid hepatic lipidosis (fatty liver disease).

test_cases.query: Why do cats purr?
test_cases.expected_answer: Cats purr for multiple reasons beyond just contentment. They purr when happy and relaxed, but also when stressed, injured, or unwell - possibly as a self-soothing mechanism. The vibrations produced during purring may promote healing of bones and tissues. Kittens purr to communicate with their mothers.

test_cases.query: Why does my cat spray urine in the house?
test_cases.expected_answer: Urine spraying is a marking behavior that can be caused by territorial stress, the presence of other cats, changes in the environment, anxiety, or medical issues like urinary tract infections. Both male and female cats can spray, though it is more common in unneutered males. Neutering often reduces spraying.

test_cases.query: How can I stop my cat from scratching furniture?
test_cases.expected_answer: To redirect scratching behavior, provide appropriate scratching posts or pads near the furniture being scratched. Use different materials (sisal, cardboard, carpet) to find your cat's preference. Make the furniture less appealing with double-sided tape. Never punish scratching - it is a natural and necessary behavior for cats.

test_cases.query: Why does my cat bite me when I pet it?
test_cases.expected_answer: This behavior is called petting-induced aggression or overstimulation. Some cats have a threshold for physical contact and will bite when they feel overstimulated. Watch for warning signs like tail twitching, skin rippling, or ears flattening. Stop petting before the cat reaches its threshold.

test_cases.query: How do I introduce a new cat to my existing cat?
test_cases.expected_answer: Introduce cats gradually by keeping the new cat in a separate room initially. Allow them to smell each other through the door and swap bedding to exchange scents. Gradually increase visual contact through a baby gate or cracked door. Only allow supervised face-to-face meetings once both cats seem calm. The process can take days to weeks.

test_cases.query: Why does my cat eat grass?
test_cases.expected_answer: Cats may eat grass to help them regurgitate indigestible material like hairballs, to obtain folic acid and other micronutrients, or simply out of instinct. While occasional grass eating is generally normal, frequent vomiting after eating grass may warrant a veterinary visit.

test_cases.query: How much sleep do cats need?
test_cases.expected_answer: Cats sleep an average of 12-16 hours per day, with some cats sleeping up to 20 hours. They are crepuscular, meaning they are most active at dawn and dusk. Senior cats and kittens tend to sleep more. Changes in sleeping patterns can indicate health issues and should be monitored.

test_cases.query: Why does my cat bring me dead animals?
test_cases.expected_answer: Cats bringing dead prey to their owners is an instinctual behavior. Theories include that cats are sharing their catch with their family group, attempting to teach hunting skills (as mother cats do with kittens), or simply bringing their prey to a safe location. It should not be punished as it is natural feline behavior.

test_cases.query: Are lilies toxic to cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Yes, lilies are extremely toxic to cats. Even small amounts of any part of the plant - petals, leaves, pollen, or water from the vase - can cause acute kidney failure. Easter lilies, tiger lilies, Asiatic lilies, and daylilies are among the most dangerous. Immediate veterinary treatment is essential.

test_cases.query: What human foods are toxic to cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Toxic human foods for cats include chocolate, onions, garlic, grapes, raisins, alcohol, caffeine, xylitol (artificial sweetener), and raw dough. Chocolate contains theobromine which can cause heart problems and seizures. Onions and garlic can damage red blood cells causing anemia.

test_cases.query: What should I do if my cat eats something poisonous?
test_cases.expected_answer: If your cat ingests something poisonous, contact your veterinarian or an emergency animal hospital immediately. You can also call the ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center. Do not induce vomiting unless specifically instructed by a veterinarian. Bring the packaging or a sample of what was ingested.

test_cases.query: Is essential oil diffusing safe around cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Many essential oils are toxic to cats because cats lack certain liver enzymes needed to metabolize them. Oils particularly dangerous to cats include tea tree, eucalyptus, citrus oils, peppermint, lavender, and cinnamon. Even diffusing these oils can cause respiratory distress in cats.

test_cases.query: Can cats eat raw fish safely?
test_cases.expected_answer: Raw fish is not recommended for cats. It can contain bacteria and parasites, and certain raw fish contains thiaminase, an enzyme that breaks down thiamine (vitamin B1). Thiamine deficiency can cause serious neurological problems. Cooked fish in moderation can be an acceptable treat.

test_cases.query: Are poinsettias dangerous for cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Poinsettias are mildly toxic to cats but are not as dangerous as commonly believed. Ingestion may cause mild mouth and stomach irritation, drooling, and occasional vomiting, but serious poisoning is rare. Other holiday plants like lilies and mistletoe are much more dangerous.

test_cases.query: Is acetaminophen (Tylenol) safe for cats?
test_cases.expected_answer: Acetaminophen is extremely toxic to cats and can be fatal even in small doses. Cats lack the necessary enzyme to metabolize acetaminophen, leading to damage of red blood cells and liver failure. Never give human pain medications to cats without veterinary guidance.
